title: 1871 primary-source field notebook
scope: Selected, traceable observations for reconstructing Chicago before the Great Fire. This is an expanding extraction, not a complete city census or a certified October 8 inventory.

books.title: Edwards’ Annual Directory of the City of Chicago, 1871
books.author: Richard Edwards, publisher
books.date_scope: 1871 directory compilation; individual entries are not an October 8 census.
books.rights: Public-domain 1871 publication; Internet Archive metadata: NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT. Digitized copy supplied by the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign.
books.bias: Commercial directory: uneven coverage, omissions, abbreviations and printing errors; named household heads and businesses do not represent every resident.

books.title: Tenth Annual Report of the Board of Public Works
books.author: Chicago Board of Public Works
books.date_scope: Fiscal year ending March 31, 1871; commissioners’ letter July 1; p. 17 adds an event on July 15. Individual sections specify their own dates.
books.rights: Public-domain 1871 municipal report; Google-digitized copy available through Internet Archive.
books.bias: Administrative self-report. Expenditure, assessment, proposal, completed work and measured observation are different kinds of evidence.

books.title: Ninth Annual Report of the Board of Public Works
books.author: Chicago Board of Public Works
books.date_scope: Fiscal year ending March 31, 1870. Earlier baseline, not an October 1871 inspection.
books.rights: Public-domain 1870 municipal publication; Internet Archive digitized copy.
books.bias: Administrative account of work. Archive metadata gives an erroneous 1861 date; the title page identifies the ninth report for the fiscal year ending March 31, 1870. Continuity into October 1871 requires checking.

method: A selective primary-source extraction. Transcription / locating text may normalize punctuation, expand abbreviations or omit surrounding text; consult the linked original scan before treating it as a verbatim quotation. Source dates, historical addresses and reporting basis stay attached to every observation. Proposed scene actions are hypotheses, not eyewitness accounts. No coordinates, footprints or October 8 actor placements are created by this notebook.
